note: Generated by tools/anatomy/build.mjs. Units are metres, Y is up, the body faces +Z, +X is the body's left. Each group has one node per side in the .glb ("biceps.L", "biceps.R"; "C" is the middle). The .glb also holds a "Skeleton" mesh and a "Skin" mesh, a smooth layer over everything.

groups.label: Chest
groups.about: The big fan-shaped muscle on the front of the ribcage (pectoralis major, with the smaller pectoralis minor beneath it). It pushes the arm forward and across the body, as in every press and fly.

groups.label: Front delts
groups.about: The front part of the shoulder muscle (anterior deltoid). It lifts the arm forward and helps in all pressing movements.

groups.label: Side delts
groups.about: The middle of the shoulder cap (lateral deltoid). It lifts the arm out to the side and gives the shoulders their width.

groups.label: Rear delts
groups.about: The back of the shoulder (posterior deltoid). It pulls the arm backwards and outwards, and works hard in rows and reverse flyes.

groups.label: Rotator cuff
groups.about: Four small muscles around the shoulder joint (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis) that hold the arm bone in its socket and rotate the arm. Mostly under the other shoulder muscles.

groups.label: Upper traps
groups.about: The upper trapezius and the levator scapulae, from the neck to the shoulder. They lift the shoulders (a shrug) and tilt the head.

groups.label: Lats
groups.about: The latissimus dorsi, the broad wing-shaped muscle of the back that runs from the spine and pelvis to the upper arm. It pulls the arm down and back in pull-ups, pulldowns and rows, and gives the back its width.

groups.label: Mid back
groups.about: The middle and lower trapezius, the rhomboids and the teres major between the shoulder blades. They pull the shoulder blades together and down and keep the shoulders from rounding forward.

groups.label: Biceps
groups.about: The muscles at the front of the upper arm (biceps brachii, brachialis and coracobrachialis). They bend the elbow and turn the forearm palm-up.

groups.label: Triceps
groups.about: The three-headed muscle at the back of the upper arm, with the small anconeus. It straightens the elbow and works in every pressing movement.

groups.label: Forearm extensors
groups.about: The muscles on the back and thumb side of the forearm, including the brachioradialis. They lift the wrist and fingers back and help in hammer curls.

groups.label: Forearm flexors
groups.about: The muscles on the palm side of the forearm. They bend the wrist and fingers and turn the forearm palm-down: your grip strength.

groups.label: Hands
groups.about: The small muscles of the palm and thumb that move the fingers. They are trained with grip work.

groups.label: Neck
groups.about: The muscles that hold and move the head: the sternocleidomastoid, the scalenes, the splenius, and the small muscles under the jaw and along the neck bones.

groups.label: Lower back
groups.about: Three columns of muscle (iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis) on either side of the spine. They straighten the back and keep it upright in deadlifts, rows and back extensions. Often called the lower back.

groups.label: Multifidus
groups.about: Short deep muscles that link each vertebra to the ones above and stabilise the spine. They lie deep under the erector spinae and matter for back health.

groups.label: Deep back
groups.about: Small deep muscles between the vertebrae and the ribs (rotatores, interspinales, serratus posterior and others). They fine-tune the position of the spine.

groups.label: Serratus
groups.about: The finger-like muscle along the side of the ribs that holds the shoulder blade against the chest. It pushes the arm forward, as at the end of a push-up.

groups.label: Abs
groups.about: The rectus abdominis, the "six-pack": the vertical muscle at the front of the abdomen. It bends the spine forward in a crunch and keeps the pelvis from tipping forward.

groups.label: Obliques
groups.about: The external obliques on the sides of the abdomen. They rotate and bend the trunk sideways and brace it in twists and side bends.

groups.label: Internal obliques
groups.about: The internal obliques, a layer under the external obliques. They rotate and bend the trunk and brace the abdomen.

groups.label: Transverse abdominis
groups.about: The deepest abdominal muscle, wrapping around the waist like a corset. It braces the abdomen and supports the spine in planks and heavy lifts.

groups.label: Quadratus lumborum
groups.about: A flat four-sided muscle between the lowest rib and the pelvis, beside the lower spine. It bends the trunk sideways and steadies the pelvis in side planks and carries.

groups.label: Intercostals
groups.about: The thin muscles between the ribs. They raise and lower the ribs when you breathe.

groups.label: Glutes
groups.about: The gluteus maximus, the largest muscle in the body and the shape of the buttock. It extends the hip in squats, deadlifts, hip thrusts and running uphill.

groups.label: Glute medius & TFL
groups.about: The gluteus medius and minimus on the side of the hip, with the tensor fasciae latae and the iliotibial band down the outer thigh. They lift the leg out to the side and keep the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.

groups.label: Deep hip rotators
groups.about: Deep muscles under the glutes (piriformis, the gemelli, the obturators and quadratus femoris). They turn the thigh outward and steady the hip joint.

groups.label: Hip flexors
groups.about: The iliacus and psoas (deep) and the sartorius, the long strap across the thigh. They lift the thigh toward the trunk in leg raises, running and climbing.

groups.label: Quadriceps
groups.about: The four muscles on the front of the thigh (rectus femoris and the three vastus muscles). They straighten the knee in squats, leg presses and lunges.

groups.label: Hamstrings
groups.about: The muscles on the back of the thigh (biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus). They bend the knee and extend the hip in leg curls and Romanian deadlifts.

groups.label: Inner thigh
groups.about: The inner-thigh muscles (the adductors, gracilis and pectineus). They pull the leg toward the middle and help in squats and deadlifts.

groups.label: Shins
groups.about: The muscles on the front of the lower leg (tibialis anterior and the toe extensors). They lift the foot and toes up toward the shin.

groups.label: Calves
groups.about: The gastrocnemius and soleus at the back of the lower leg, with the deeper muscles beside them. They point the foot down in calf raises, walking and jumping.

groups.label: Feet
groups.about: The small muscles of the sole and the top of the foot that move the toes and support the arch.

notIncluded: the muscles of the face and scalp (masseter, temporalis, frontalis ...)
